question: The Narmada or Nerbudda is a river in central India that empties into the Arabian Sea in the state of _______.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Gujarat**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Narmada River, also known as the Rewa, is one of the major rivers in central India.
 
• It flows westwards over a length of approximately 1,312 kilometers (815 miles).
 
• The river originates from the Amarkantak plateau in the state of Madhya Pradesh.
 
• It eventually drains into the Arabian Sea in the state of Gujarat.
 
• The Narmada is known for its religious significance and is considered one of the seven holy rivers of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Geographical Importance:**

 
 
• The Narmada River basin spans over the states of Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, and Gujarat.
 
• It forms the traditional boundary between North India and South India.
 
 
 
• **Religious Significance:**
 
 
• The Narmada is worshipped as a goddess by many people, and it is believed that a dip in the river can cleanse one of all sins.
 
• Several ghats and temples are situated along its banks, making it a pilgrimage site.
 
 
 
• **Hydroelectric Projects:**
 
 
• Major dams on the Narmada include the Sardar Sarovar Dam, which is one of the largest dams in India.
 
• These projects are crucial for irrigation, water supply, and hydroelectric power generation.
 
 
 
• **Ecological Aspects:**
 
 
• The Narmada Valley is home to diverse flora and fauna, including several endangered species.
 
• Efforts are being made to conserve the river ecosystem amidst growing developmental challenges.
